# Illumination and Tone Shading Models
## Overview
Illumination and Tone Shading Models provide non-photorealistic lighting cues to enhance the visual clarity and artistic style of volume renderings [G]. Unlike photometric models that simulate physical light transport, these methods map geometric or scalar properties to pre-defined color variations, prioritizing interpretability and aesthetic control over physical accuracy [G]. They are distinct from [Geometric Buffers](781-geometric-buffers-g-buffers.md) by focusing on color modulation rather than depth/normal encoding, and from [Base Gaseous Illumination Renderer](794-base-gaseous-illumination-renderer.md) by incorporating directed shading components [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Illustrative and non-photorealistic volume rendering](40-illustrative-and-non-photorealistic-volume-rendering.md) for the family's shared principles. [G]

## Subtopics

[Lit Sphere Shading](785-lit-sphere-shading.md) uses a pre-shaded sphere image as a lookup table for view-dependent lighting. It sets itself apart from [Volume Illustration Tone Shading](805-volume-illustration-tone-shading.md) and [Vignette Shading](1830-vignette-shading.md) by relying on a geometric sphere proxy rather than scalar field properties or screen-space effects, and from [Blinn-Phong Toon Shading](4708-blinn-phong-toon-shading.md) by encoding pre-computed artistic styles rather than computing analytical geometric light interactions. Choose this for stylized, view-dependent lighting that rotates with the camera. [G]

[Volume Illustration Tone Shading](805-volume-illustration-tone-shading.md) combines gaseous illumination with directed shading based on the signed dot product between the gradient and light vector, using continuous warm/cool color interpolation. It sets itself apart from [Lit Sphere Shading](785-lit-sphere-shading.md) and [Vignette Shading](1830-vignette-shading.md) by using complex transfer functions and signed dot products rather than geometric proxies or screen-space effects. Choose this for realistic yet stylized volume rendering with clear directional cues. [G]

[Vignette Shading](1830-vignette-shading.md) applies a cubic vignette effect based on the alignment between ray direction and the z-axis. It sets itself apart from [Lit Sphere Shading](785-lit-sphere-shading.md) and [Volume Illustration Tone Shading](805-volume-illustration-tone-shading.md) because it operates on the final rendered image based on pixel position and camera geometry rather than modulating volume sample gradients or surface normals. Choose this for adding depth and focus to the volume. [G]

[Blinn-Phong Toon Shading](4708-blinn-phong-toon-shading.md) is a toon-shaded variant of Blinn-Phong that posterizes diffuse lighting and harshly cuts specular reflections. It sets itself apart from [Lit Sphere Shading](785-lit-sphere-shading.md) which maps lighting to a sphere texture, or [Volume Illustration Tone Shading](805-volume-illustration-tone-shading.md) which uses complex transfer functions, by relying on simple arithmetic thresholds applied to the dot products of the normal and light vectors. Choose this for discrete, cartoon-like lighting effects. [G]

[Volumetric Toon Shading](5276-volumetric-toon-shading.md) simulates toon shading using a 3D normal map and hardware texture combiners. It sets itself apart from polygonal toon-shading by operating entirely on a per-fragment basis using a 3D normal map and hardware texture combiners, decoupling the illumination model from physical light transport to produce discrete, stylized tones. Choose this for efficient, hardware-accelerated cel shading without explicit surface vertices. [G]

[Lighting Transfer Function with Gradient Aligned Sampling](7966-lighting-transfer-function-with-gradient-aligned-sampling.md) enhances material boundaries by using two scalar samples taken along the normalized gradient direction as inputs to a 2D lighting transfer function, while the center sample is used for color/opacity. It sets itself apart from other illumination models by explicitly aligning sampling with the gradient direction to capture boundary details. Choose this when precise boundary highlighting is required. [G]

### Banks Illumination Model for Curves
Uses the illumination model for curves of Banks [12] in the rendering to provide a better sense of curvature [S1, unofficial]. Line bundles can be more opaque in this variant [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of non-photorealistic volume rendering emerged to address the ambiguity of standard volume rendering, where internal structures can be hard to distinguish [G]. Early work focused on enhancing edge detection and silhouette rendering [G]. The specific illumination models in this family, such as Lit Sphere Shading and Volume Illustration Tone Shading, were developed to provide intuitive lighting cues that help viewers perceive shape and depth in volumetric data without the computational cost of full global illumination [G]. These techniques are widely used in medical visualization, scientific data exploration, and artistic volume rendering [G].
